sources.text:
Hailuoto (Finnish: [ˈhɑi̯ˌluo̯to]; Swedish: Karlö) is a Finnish island in the northern Baltic Sea and a municipality in Northern Ostrobothnia region. The population of Hailuoto is 912 (December 31, 2025), making it the smallest municipality in Northern Ostrobothnia and the former Oulu Province in terms of population. The municipality covers an area of 205.65 km2 (79.40 sq mi) (excluding sea areas) of which 1.70 km2 (0.66 sq mi) is inland water (January 1, 2018). The population density is 4.43/km2 (11.5/sq mi). Of all the Finnish sea islands, Hailuoto is the third largest after Fasta Åland and Kimitoön.
Hailuoto lies opposite the city of Oulu in the Gulf of Bothnia. The distance between Oulu and Hailuoto is 53 kilometres (33 mi), and the sea area between them is called Luodonselkä (literally "open water of the islet").
Land in the region is constantly rising due to post-glacial rebound. It is estimated that the first parts of Hailuoto appeared from the Baltic Sea about 1700 years ago. The current island of Hailuoto was formed from many smaller islands. Two large sections, Santonen and Hanhinen merged into the main island (Luoto) only about two centuries ago. stops.name: Hailuoto
stops.detail: Hailuoto ist eine finnische Insel in der nördlichen Ostsee und eine Gemeinde in der Region Nordostrobothnia. Die Einwohnerzahl von Hailuoto beträgt 912 und ist damit die kleinste Gemeinde in Nordostrobothnia und der ehemaligen Provinz Oulu. Die Gemeinde umfasst eine Fläche von 205,65 km2, davon 1,70 km2 Binnenwasser. Die Bevölkerungsdichte beträgt 4,43/km2. Von allen finnischen Meeresinseln ist Hailuoto die drittgrößte nach Fasta Åland und Kimitoön.
